args.notes: System spec: 32 requests issued at once per 1 us tick, all 32 must return within 0.44 us (p99). So need throughput >= 32 Msps AND batch latency <= 0.44 us for a batch of 32 -> per-request latency budget ~0.44us; pipelined/multi-lane families likely needed (32 lanes or high II=1 throughput with short latency). Accuracy: max_abs_err <= 2^-12 = 0.000244141, so accuracy_bits >= 12. Objective: minimise luts_plus_ffs (HV ref 4000), maximise accuracy_bits (HV ref 12). Selection rule: min luts_plus_ffs among feasible. L1 screens the system constraint with an analytic bound; keep the shortlist diverse in family (iterative, unrolled_k, pipelined, pipelined_m) so L2 can re-select on simulated p99.

args.lesson: multiaxis_control (32 req/tick, 1 MHz, p99 batch <= 0.44 us, err <= 2^-12, min LUTs+FFs): the whole feasible front was pipelined_m with m=4 (4 lanes x II=1 gives ~90 Msps and ~0.40 us batch). Full 400-eval run_dse gave 24 feasible non-dominated designs; L2 simulation of top 8 shifted sys_p99_batch_us up by ~0.011 us vs the L1 analytic bound (0.385->0.395) but all passed and the winner was unchanged. Cheapest feasible design was data_width=19, n_iter=15, guards 2/2, trunc: 1340 LUTs+FFs, 13.7 bits. L3/L4/L5 returned no recorded data (no_measured_data) for this design, so no winner change and no reexplore. Lesson: for latency-bound system specs, spend the full L1 budget in one run_dse and simulate top_k=8; the analytic bound is a slight underestimate of p99 but not enough to flip the min-area winner.
